body:
I sounds like something is wrong. The cakephp test suite generates quite a few queries and it runs under 5 seconds for over 600 tests. Can you help us debug your problem? Enable the queries logging and try to pin point where is the slowness.

If you don't do `pr($articles)` is it still slow?
I'm assuming this is with the ORM in 3.0?

Yes, this is in 3.0 with the new preview realise.

And yes, I had $articles as plural because I was just testing this with find all and find first.

Please find attached:

1) My ArticlesController file.
2) The SQL dump.

I have tried this on a fresh install of Cake 3 and had the same issues.  Time was between 9 - 17 seconds!

Would be interested to hear if you guys have the same issue.  Let me know anyway.

https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/90804133/ArticlesController.php
https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/90804133/articles-dump.sql

If you don't, I can load this up to a web server so you can see it in effect there.
The time it takes for me is below 5 ms. How does development environment is? Do you use a virtual machine or something like that? Can you tell us exactly what php version are you using?

Using Ubuntu 12.10 wth PHP Version 5.4.6-1ubuntu1.5.

I have a test server with PHP 5.4 on it, I will load this up tomorrow to test there.

Not sure whether this is the same problem, but I'm experiencing something similar, it takes around 7 seconds for me on a local Windows development system, it's working fine on the production system however.

Dev: Windows 7 x64, PHP 5.5.6
Production: Ubuntu (not sure about the version, was just moved to a new server), PHP 5.5.5-nmm1

I've tracked it down to the establishing of the PDO connection (1.8 seconds) in `PDODriverTrait::_connect()` and the information schema querying (5.2 seconds) in `\Database\Schema\Collection::describe()`. The former gets a major speedup (down to 0.001 seconds) when using `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost` (not sure yet why, the DNS table that needs to be looked up isn't that big), and the latter is because of the huge funked up information schema, it's already horribly slow when queried directly. Not sure whether there's any room for optimizations of the query (it's the join that really slows it down).

Maybe this is of any help.
@ndm2 What happens when you use 2.x with similar settings (localhost)? Just curious.
I tried 127.0.0.1 instead of localhost, but still the same issues for me unfortunutely.  I will be loading this to a server and see if it makes a difference.
I cannot reproduce this issue either on ubuntu 13.04 with PHP 5.4.9 and MySql 5.5.34.
@cakecoded Are you using the 3.0-dev1 release or 3.0 branch HEAD? (Though it's unlikely to make a difference.)
@josegonzalez Same problem with PDO in 2.x, in my case that's really something specific to the system, definitely not cake's fault.
@ADmad - I am using the 3.0-dev1 release.  It isn't just find()->first that is slow, even findById() is slow.  Still doing some more research into this one, will keep you posted on it.

The first find on a table will do schema reflection table. We've not yet built out the schema reflection caching features entirely. So 3.0.0-dev will be a bit slow as each request will re-do the schema reflection.

You are right Mark!  I did two find requests:
FIRST: float(12.356188058853) 
SECOND: float(0.0010201930999756) 

So the first one was slow, the second was fast!  I will get the latest repo and see if it is any faster.
Cool, this will get resolved as we add schema caching. I'm going to close this for now.
